title: TCL 115" C7K 4K QD-Mini LED (2025) $11,910.40 + Delivery ($0 C&C) @ Harvey Norman
body:

BTW, Weight (kg) 229.3

[damian1079] I knew building my house with quadruple brick would pay off eventually..
[MrFrugalSpend] maybe not so much with quadruple brick which would be very stable… but contrary to popular belief, bricks are quite weak laterally, and require brick ties back to the frame just to stay standing or engaged piers - it's the timber or steel stud frame + bracing that has the strength
[cmoddoo] The other three layers of brick will be cheering on the single internal leaf bricks to support the TV

[camshandez] Seated 3.5 metres away from 115" screen is just on the THX 40 Degrees field of view recommended.

[mafmouf] You could possibly get HN to toss in a 65 to 140in wall mount with the $11k spend.
[reece8] thanks that does look like a monster rack! that means I've gotta remove the old up to 90inch rack, and replace it with this one, anybody have experience doing this, assume will leave a bunch of holes in the wall that the TV would cover up anyway.
[tunzafun001] Check your electricity cost to see what this bad boy will cost to run over the year…
[Lucille Bluth] Worked it out for my LG CX 65"
LG CX 65": 250 kWh/year
This TV: 1,100 kWh/year
Difference: 850 kWh/year more
That's about 4.4× the electricity consumption, or roughly 340% more
Average daily use works out to about 3.0 kWh/day versus 0.68 kWh/day for the LG.
If electricity costs $0.30/kWh, that's roughly $330/year for this TV versus $75/year for the LG.
Less of a concern in my case with solar battery.
[tunzafun001] Just know the published figures are a bit "light on", and based on basic sdr using no features at basic brightness.
If you are watching HDR Netflix.. Basically double the figure.
Our LG 55 OLED is published as 90-170watts. But plugged in a power meter and it is constantly bouncing off 300 watts.
Then, I don't know where you are still getting 30c/ kWh for power. Double that rate here during usual tv use hours, which is peak.
Summary, I'd double those figures, then double them again for post July 1 power rates (if you didn't have a battery).
Meaning the average 8 -10hr tv watcher will use an extra approx$2 -$3 of power per day,. $14 - $20 per week, $700 - $1000 ish per year in power use.
Not up to me to decide your spending. Go for it. Just some people don't make the connection as to why their power bill is $240> more for the quarter.
P.S. I use a projector for big screen viewing. It uses half the power of the 55 OLED TV (but doesn't have the same peak brightness or definition)…but thats how movies should feel for me.
[Lucille Bluth] Then, I don't know where you are still getting 30c/ kWh for power
I'm currently on 24c/kWh in metro VIC.
https://ibb.co/rGvBnj2M
It is not even the cheapest inc daily supply charge with only 1c FIT, just wanted OVOs three free hour period to fully charged my battery every day during winter.
Good write up otherwise. Just FYI I am not interested in this tv - partner said NO lmao
